column4: Every chart you will ever open tells the same story in three parts. Price moves between a floor and a ceiling, it drifts in a trend, and volume tells you which of those moves to actually believe. Watch the ball bounce between the two lines on screen. Get comfortable reading those three things and a chart stops looking like noise and starts looking like a map. Let's walk through each one.

Start with the floor and the ceiling. Support is a price level where buying pressure tends to stop a decline, the floor where demand steps back in. Resistance is the ceiling, a level where selling pressure stalls a rise. Watch the animated line on screen bounce up off support and get turned away at resistance. These levels form because the market remembers them. Where buyers showed up before, they tend to show up again. This chart is illustrative, it is the shape of the idea, not a real quote.

Now zoom out and you will see direction. There are only three. An uptrend is a staircase up, higher highs and higher lows. A downtrend is the mirror image, lower highs and lower lows. And when price goes nowhere in particular, that is a sideways range. Look at the three motifs on screen, the climb, the descent, and the flat hallway. In an uptrend you draw a trendline by connecting the higher lows. In a downtrend you connect the lower highs. And remember, no trend lasts forever.

Here is the piece that separates a real move from a fake one, volume. Volume is simply the number of shares traded in a period. Look at the bars under the price line. When price pushes through a level on rising volume, that move has conviction behind it, real buyers or sellers showing up. When price drifts through on thin, weak volume, stay skeptical, that breakout can fail and snap right back. Volume does not predict, it confirms.

Your turn to train your eye. On screen you will see a small price chart. Decide, is it an uptrend, a downtrend, or a sideways range? Tap your answer and you will get instant feedback, then the next chart loads. Work through all three and check your score. Naming the trend quickly is a real skill, and it comes straight from reps.

Let's make support and resistance stick. Sort the cards yourself. Each one describes either the floor, support, or the ceiling, resistance. Tap a card, then drop it in the column where it belongs. Support is green, that is the floor where buyers step in. Resistance is red, the ceiling where sellers take over. Get all eight sorted and you will have both definitions locked in.
Five quick questions to lock it all in. Answer each one to earn your points for the lesson.

Let's carry the essentials with you. Support is the floor, resistance is the ceiling. Trends come in three flavors, up, down, and sideways, and you draw the line along the higher lows or the lower highs. Volume confirms which moves to trust, and a breakout is a decisive close through a level. Next up in Lesson three point one, we build on this foundation with chart patterns and indicators, the recurring shapes and tools that turn these raw levels into real signals.
